findings.detail: MISSING: the page recommends a reorder - "3 parts at or below the reorder threshold. Order them before the next shift planning so they arrive before they hit zero" and an "Order 3 low parts" action - and never states how long they take to arrive. The row's gloss is exact: a reorder point without lead time is half a recommendation, because the whole question is whether ordering now is early enough. SCOPE, CHECKED BEFORE PROPOSING A FIX: `inventory_items` has NO lead-time column at all (only min_qty), so this is not a rendering bug and a display-only fix would be fabricating a number. It needs a schema column plus supplier data - a decision about what the platform collects, which is Ian's call, not a defect to patch. METHOD: the page is walked signed-in at 1280x1600, given 9s to settle, and its rendered innerText is matched against patterns HARVESTED FROM A LIVE RENDER - never invented at the desk. Each check records the exact string it matched (`saw`), so this verdict can be audited without re-running it, and `--selftest` plants a satisfying AND a violating text per check so one that cannot fire is caught before it banks anything. RAILS THAT SHAPED THIS WALK: (1) a qualifier must sit NEAR the figure it qualifies - the trend check first went green on 'calendar days between failures', which is MTBF's basis on another card; (2) `near()` scans EVERY anchor occurrence, because anchoring on the first match failed skillmatrix's real '19 of 25 possible' on the source chip's earlier 'skill badges'; (3) where a page prints a claim in a fixed phrase, match the PHRASE - '114 of 409 ran late' cannot be confused with the '0 of 30' asset count one clause earlier; (4) the check must be the ROW'S oracle, not a weaker cousin - 5 of 18 cells were LEFT OWED rather than banked on half their claim.

The oracle guards a specific confusion - a unit cost rendered where a total value belongs, or the reverse, which misstates the worth of a store by the quantity factor. The precondition is that the platform holds a cost, and it does not: no column matching unit_cost or unit_price exists on any inventory table. The model is a QUANTITY ledger, not a valuation one: it tracks qty_on_hand, min_qty, unit (the unit of MEASURE, such as pcs or litres - not a currency), and movements as qty_change with a running qty_after. There is therefore no figure on this surface that a reader could mistake for money. This is consistent with the platform's stance elsewhere and is not an oversight: project-report's own standards footer states that 'the platform holds no cost ledger', which is why it refuses to compute CPI. The oracle guards a specific staleness: a part with no recent movement showing an old 'last used' date as though it were current, which would tell a storekeeper the shelf is active when it has not been touched in a year. The precondition is that such a date is DISPLAYED, and it is not - searched the page for any rendered last-used, last-movement or never-used string and found zero. The timestamps present in the source are internal: updated_at is written on save and used for optimistic-concurrency detection of a parallel edit (inventory.html:1455-1469), never painted as a freshness claim. So there is no figure here that could misrepresent its own age. REPLACEMENT EVIDENCE: the freshness signals this page DOES render are derived, not stored, so they cannot go stale by construction - is_out_of_stock is qty_on_hand <= 0 and is_low_stock is min_qty > 0 AND qty_on_hand <= min_qty (documented at inventory.html:752-753), both computed from the current quantity at read time. And the movement history that WOULD date a part is fully intact should it ever be surfaced: 453 transactions, every one carrying created_at, with the last qty_after reconciling to on-hand for 81 of 81 items. This row must be re-walked if a last-used column is added to the list.

findings.detail: FAILS, AND THE UNIFORMITY IS WHAT MAKES IT CREDIBLE RATHER THAN NOISE. Measured INSIDE the opened dialog only, so V2's numbers belong to V2: the lens resolves the largest visible [role=dialog]/modal/overlay and scopes every query to it, rather than measuring the whole document and attributing the page's V1 chrome to the modal. MEASURED at 390 CSS px (layout width read back as 384, because this display is dpr 0.667 and browser_resize takes PHYSICAL pixels): **30 of 43 interactive controls in the part-modal present an activation target under 44x44 CSS px** - and the height histogram is a single bucket, **{36: 30}**. Every one is exactly 36px tall, 148-214px wide, and every one carries the same class: `button.asset-tag`. THAT IS ONE COMPONENT, NOT THIRTY DEFECTS, AND ONE CSS FIX: a min-height on .asset-tag. A scattered set of heights would suggest measurement error; a single 36px bucket across 30 instances of one class is a design token 8px under the floor. MEASURED ON THE ACTIVATION TARGET, not the element box - inputs resolve to closest('label') where one exists, which is the distinction that produced seven fabricated defects earlier in this bank. These 30 are buttons measured on themselves, so the resolution does not soften them. WHY IT MATTERS IN THIS MODAL SPECIFICALLY: these chips link a spare part to the assets it fits, in a form a technician fills on a phone while standing at a machine. Thirty adjacent 36px targets is where a mis-tap attaches the part to the wrong asset - and the wrong linkage is invisible afterwards, because the part will look correctly registered. THRESHOLD 44x44 per WCAG 2.5.5, tested at 43.5 to absorb sub-pixel layout. TO FINISH (batched per A15): min-height: 44px on .asset-tag, then re-walk. The V1 surface of this page passes this oracle (0 of 44 undersized), so this is modal-only and the page's general density is not the problem.

findings.detail: FAILS: 30 of 43 effective tap targets inside #part-modal are under the platform's own 44px floor - button.asset-tag 195.9x36 via own box; button.asset-tag 153x36 via own box; button.asset-tag 148x36 via own box; button.asset-tag 165x36 via own box; button.asset-tag 214x36 via own box. THIS IS MEASURED ON THE SAME RULER THAT PASSED 750 of 750 AT PAGE LEVEL: the rule is ported verbatim from the V1 prover, so these are controls the platform's own standard would reject, in a view V1 never opened.  HOW IT WAS MEASURED, and why these rows sat owed for so long: CJ was measured platform-wide at V1 and banked there, and V2/V3 stayed owed for ONE reason - nobody could open those views. Resolving all 15 dialog open paths (each read from SOURCE, never matched by label) removed that blocker, and the same measurements now run inside the OPENED dialog. The open-path table lives in tools/dialog_targets.mjs, shared with the modal-exit prover so the two cannot drift apart. SCOPED TO THE DIALOG, NOT THE PAGE, which is the whole point: a dialog OVERLAYS the page, so measuring document.body with a sheet open would re-measure V1 and bank it as V2 - the one-reading-for-every-layer error this bank has already paid for once. Every measurement is rooted at the dialog element. Overflow compares each visible descendant's right edge against the dialog's own content box, with a 1px tolerance (an earlier arc counted a 0.109px abutment as occlusion) and honours overflow-x auto/scroll/hidden/clip on an ancestor INSIDE the dialog, because a deliberately scrollable panel is not a defect. THE TAP-TARGET RULE IS PORTED VERBATIM FROM THE V1 PROVER, NOT REINVENTED, and that correction is why this number means anything. The first cut omitted four of V1's exclusions - sr-only, disabled, the actionable check, and the WCAG 2.5.5 inline-link-in-prose exception - and REPLACED a control's rect with its label instead of UNIONING them. Applying a stricter standard at V2 than at V1 does not find defects, it manufactures a difference between the two views and calls it one. With V1's exact rule restored the count came back IDENTICAL, which is what makes these findings real rather than an artifact: they are measured on the same ruler that banked 750/750 at page level. SCOPE: 390px only, the mobile-first width. w641/w1280 for these views are NOT claimed by this run. Two of the 15 dialogs are UNGRADED with their reason recorded rather than counted - resume's #review-sheet has no read-only path in (it needs the upload -> resume-extract pipeline, which WRITES) and hive's #handover-sheet cannot be reached at all. The walk is NON-WRITING: it opens a dialog, measures, and presses Escape.

findings.title: FALSE GREEN WITHDRAWN - reduced_motion was banked on a page-level boolean and this page never honoured the preference: 8 part cards kept sliding (slide-in) - 8 normally, 8 still under reduce
findings.detail: The row claimed the page honours prefers-reduced-motion. It did not. The evidence behind the claim was live-state-runner.js returning ok: declaresGuard, a single boolean meaning 'somewhere in this document there is an @media (prefers-reduced-motion) rule' - which says nothing about whether the rule covers the elements that actually move. 8 part cards kept sliding (slide-in) - 8 normally, 8 still under reduce. Withdrawn rather than silently re-walked, because a green that falls without a recorded reason is how a ratchet becomes a rebaseline. The defect is now fixed and the row re-earned against an emulated media flip with the running-animation sets compared, and the lens that produced the false green has been rebuilt to report the unguarded SET per element and self-tested 4 ways in both directions.

findings.detail: MEASURED INSIDE THIS VIEW, with tools/prove_view_contrast.mjs - 34 of 37 drivable registry views carried text to measure, ZERO failing. ★WHY A VIEW-SCOPED PROVER HAD TO BE BUILT FOR THIS: a page-level sweep of all 22 pages (tools/prove_page_contrast.mjs) found the platform clean and settled NOTHING here, because every owed contrast row in these banks is authored against V2 or V3 - the dialogs - while their V1 siblings were already green. Banking a page-default reading onto a V2 row is the one-measurement-swept-two-views error that has already put 14 rows in this bank carrying another view's verdict. The view is opened through tools/dialog_targets.mjs, the same shared registry ten other provers use, so the view graded here is the view they grade. WCAG 2.x is measured with the composited probe: the background is blended UP the ancestor chain, because a translucent tint over a dark card is not the colour the stylesheet names, and text over a gradient is recorded as UNMEASURABLE rather than being compared against a canvas it never sits on - the shape that once reported ratio exactly 1.00 for perfectly legible text. NOT BANKED: this view yielded ZERO measurable samples (53 unmeasurable), so there is no denominator and a pass would be vacuous. The cause is structural rather than a probe fault, and it was verified by tracing the paint chain: the dialog's inner card is a TRANSLUCENT GRADIENT - linear-gradient(145deg, rgba(42,61,88,0.6) ...) - over a rgba(0,0,0,0.75) scrim over the page. WCAG 2.x is a ratio between TWO colours, and there is no single background colour here to be the second one. THE APCA SIBLING OF THIS ROW IS NOT AFFECTED and was measured normally, because that lens averages the gradient's stops instead of demanding one flat colour - which is why the platform treats APCA as the primary contrast oracle on this dark shell. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: sample the RENDERED PIXELS around each glyph from a screenshot of this view, which is the only way to obtain the real second colour behind text that sits on a gradient. That is a buildable instrument, not a ceiling - it is simply not built yet, and this row stays owed until it is.

findings.title: NOT BANKED - why_refused needs a refusal INDUCED and the probe induced none (refusedCalls 0, vacuous). Probe built; its submit-finder is the remaining work
findings.detail: A REFUSAL DOES NOT EXIST ON A SETTLED PAGE, so this oracle cannot be observed - it has to be INDUCED. comprehension().refusals returns an EMPTY ARRAY on all 20 pages for exactly that reason: nothing has been refused yet. Banking '0 of 0 refusals lack a reason' would be vacuously true, and banking it as a pass is how coverage improves by deleting obligations. So a probe was built for it - window.__wh7.whyRefused() - which answers every mutating verb locally with a 403 in the PostgREST permission shape (code 42501, 'permission denied for table'), drives a submit, and reads what the page TELLS the person. No write is forwarded, so nothing reaches the shared test database. THE ORACLE IT ENCODES, which is worth keeping even though the row is still owed: 403 IS NOT 401. Under RLS a 403 means the session is ALIVE and this action is not permitted, so 'sign in again' is the wrong answer and sends someone to fix the one thing that is not broken. This platform already learned that in the other direction - a 42501 once told a signed-in buyer their session had expired. A good refusal names the PERMISSION or the ROLE. The probe therefore reports saysRefused, namesReason and blamesSession separately, and requires (saysRefused OR namesReason) AND NOT blamesSession. WHY THE ROW IS STILL OWED, stated exactly: refusedCalls came back 0 on all four pages plus logbook and pm-scheduler, so NOTHING was ever refused and the verdict is stamped vacuous:true with ok forced to null rather than false. The probe is honest about having no subject; it is not reporting a pass. TWO CONCRETE DEFECTS IN THE PROBE, both found by measuring rather than reasoning, and both fixed or named: (1) it reused m() and navigatesAway(), which are LOCAL to overflow()/tapTargets() in that file, so it threw ReferenceError - and the crash hit report-sender, the ONE page of six that had any submit candidate at all. A staged try/catch reporting CRASH_AT:probe instead of a bare REJ is what separated a broken probe from a blocked page; without it, six pages looked uniformly refused when the probe had simply crashed. Both scope bugs are fixed. (2) THE TARGET-FINDER IS TOO LOOSE and that is the remaining work: its selector list includes [id*="send"], which matched 'report-sender-source-chip' - the page's own NAME contains 'send'. A source chip submits nothing, which is precisely why refusedCalls stayed 0 on the one page that looked promising. TO FINISH THIS ROW: replace substring id matching with real submit semantics - button[type=submit] inside a form, or a control whose onclick names a save/send/submit FUNCTION (the same read-the-markup approach that fixed the V2 openers after class-name guesses all missed) - and drive it from inside an OPEN form view, since these list surfaces have no submit control at all. Opening the form first was tried here (openUseModal / openModal / openDetail) and still yielded 0 refused calls, so the modal's own save control needs naming per page rather than discovering generically. Row stays owed.
findings.observed: whyRefused(): refusedCalls 0, submitUsed null (report-sender matched 'report-sender-source-chip' via a loose [id*=send] selector), ok null, vacuous true. Also fixed two ReferenceErrors from reusing function-local helpers (m, navigatesAway) at module scope.

findings.title: FAILS: with 14 of this page's reads answered 403/42501, it says NOTHING AT ALL - the body text is 1858 characters before the refusal and 958 after, and no new sentence explains anything.  WHAT THIS ORACLE IS REALLY FOR, and the good news first: it checks that a refusal names PERMISSION rather than I
findings.detail: FAILS: with 14 of this page's reads answered 403/42501, it says NOTHING AT ALL - the body text is 1858 characters before the refusal and 958 after, and no new sentence explains anything.  WHAT THIS ORACLE IS REALLY FOR, and the good news first: it checks that a refusal names PERMISSION rather than IDENTITY, because this platform has already shipped that exact inversion - a 42501 rendered as 'your session has expired', which sends a signed-IN person to re-authenticate for a problem authentication cannot fix, and 401/403 collapsed into one message so neither audience got a true statement. ZERO of the 16 graded pages made that mistake on this run. utils.js:1607 whIsAuthFailure() is why: it returns FALSE for status 403 with the comment 'authenticated, and refused. Not a session problem', and documents 42501 as insufficient_privilege. That discrimination is holding. HOW THE REFUSAL WAS INDUCED, and why it is the real branch: every Supabase REST read is answered with the body PostgREST actually sends for a row-level-security refusal - HTTP 403 with {"code":"42501","message":"permission denied for table"} - so the page's own error handling takes the same path it would in production. The patch is on window.fetch, NOT page.route, because a warm service worker serves from cache and bypasses route interception; it is installed with addInitScript in a context closed after each page so it cannot leak. NON-WRITING: it makes a READ return 403. THE INJECTION PROVES ITSELF: every intercepted call increments a counter, and a page where the counter is zero is UNGRADED rather than judged. That guard exists because the first version of this prover silently did nothing - a regex written inside a template literal collapsed to one that terminates at its second character, so the init script was a SyntaxError, every read succeeded normally, and the prover reported 'the reads were all refused and the page said nothing' while nothing had been refused at all. Hit counts on this run ranged from 8 to 42 per page. AND THE SIGNAL MUST APPEAR: the same page is read WITHOUT the injection first, and if its ordinary copy already matches the refusal vocabulary the page is UNGRADED - which is exactly what happened to skillmatrix, whose normal text contains a matching phrase. Without that control a page whose everyday copy happens to say 'cannot' would pass for free. THE SYNTHESIS - THIS IS ONE MISSING SURFACE, NOT 15 PAGE BUGS. Of 16 graded pages: 13 said NOTHING AT ALL when every read was refused, 2 showed only a GENERIC error ('Analysis failed, check console'; 'Achievements failed to load.'), and 1 passed. The platform already has the pieces - a central WRITE-failure message and the correct 401-vs-403 discriminator in utils.js - but there is no equivalent on the READ path, so a refused read renders as dashes or blanks with no explanation. On logbook the numbers '516 entries 30 machines 6 open' became '- entries - machines - open' with the body text identical to the character (1107 before and after) and not one word about why. A person cannot tell 'there is no data' from 'the load failed' from 'you are not allowed', and those three call for three different actions. THE FIX IS ONE ADOPTION, not 15 edits: give the read path the same treatment the write path already has. This independently reproduces a finding already recorded as 'the message already exists; the gap is ADOPTION on the read path'. SCOPE: V1, the page as it loads, and READ refusal only - a refused WRITE is a different path with its own central message, and is not claimed here. 5 of the 22 pages are excluded from the sweep because they are public or have no authenticated read to refuse. The walk is NON-WRITING.

scenarios.question: mistakes, reversals and interruption - and after a slow tap: did my thing land?
scenarios.oracle: after a slow action the person can tell whether it landed, without guessing

evidence.asserts: after acting, the person is told whether it landed
evidence.checked: MEASURED with tools/prove_did_it_land.mjs: 26 controls driven, 26 pass, 0 fail, 0 ungraded - and NO WRITE REACHED THE DATABASE, every mutating request intercepted and answered in-page. ★THE QUESTION IS THE ONE A PERSON ASKS WITH THEIR THUMB STILL ON THE SCREEN: did that land? A surface that takes a press and says nothing leaves them to guess, and the guess is almost always 'do it again' - which is how a duplicate gets created. So the oracle is not 'did the write succeed' but 'was the person TOLD', and the two come apart exactly when the network is slow. ★AND IT IS ANSWERED BY ACTING, WHICH IS WHY THE INTERCEPTION MATTERS MORE THAN THE VERDICT. Every other check in this bank can be answered by looking; this one presses real controls on a live product. The requests are counted and answered inside the page so the probe cannot perform the thing it means to observe - a discipline this platform bought the hard way, when an earlier sweep hunting for a refusal ACTIVATED A SUCCESS because its filter excluded delete/pay but not save/generate.
